rationale: D7 K1 CORRECTED (charter §18, task-21; arm-A measured): the call-emission gate refuses a target that can never be a declared name — a C KEYWORD — and KEEPS every other spelling. The first K1 also refused NON-IDENTIFIER spellings; the arm-A after-run proved that half wrong: of 43 withdrawn calls rows, 40 were the predicted recovery garbage but 3 were REAL name-model resolutions — calls to `$`-containing identifiers whose declarations the analyzer itself publishes (Cython's generated `__Pyx_ImportType_$cyversion`/`__Pyx_ImportFromPxd_$cyversion` in `Cython/Utility/ImportExport.c`), so the broad guard removed resolutions to enforce a spelling rule. Narrowed to KEYWORD-ONLY: a keyword cannot be declared anywhere (declaration extraction refused keywords since CGD22; corpus-wide `#define <keyword>` = 0), so the keyword half cannot withdraw a resolution; a non-identifier spelling is not disqualified, so the `$` call in this fixture is now a POSITIVE control that must keep publishing. SUBJECTS: (1) a keyword callee from macro-with-statement recovery — SuiteSparse CHOLMOD writes `DEBUG (if (cond) fn ())`, recovery published `calls ... -> if` (34 unresolved + 1 ambiguous at whole population after the class-boundary correction); (2) the OLD non-identifier subject, kept as the over-reach control. RED measured before the first guard landed (7 calls rows incl. `-> if`); the keyword row is now forbidden, the `$` row is now expected. Fixture pins BOTH directions: five controls + the `$` spelling must publish, and the keyword must not; a guard that suppresses wholesale or over-reaches fails here.
